summary: Flaky/RED: web/storefront session-cap tests time out — 20,050 sessions against vitest's 5s default
description:
Found on 2026-08-08 while gating **TKT-198**, and **confirmed pre-existing and unrelated** to it.

`web/storefront/test/session.test.ts` — four cases in the `customer sessions` describe block fail
under `make check`:

```
× bounds the map globally, across unlimited distinct principals   14945ms
× refuses a new session at capacity rather than evicting a live one 8668ms
× lets a customer at their own cap rotate a session even when the map is full 12440ms
× accepts new sessions again once capacity frees up                8060ms
Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
```

**Proof it is not TKT-198's:** TKT-198's diff is Go and shell only — it touches no TypeScript
(`scripts/smoke.sh`, `services/commerce/internal/bulkrefund/runner_smoke_test.go`, and a new Go
test). With those changes **stashed**, on a tree identical to `origin/main` for all code paths,
`npx vitest run test/session.test.ts` reported **4 failed | 25 passed** in 51s. The gate is red on
`main` for this too.

**Mechanism.** `MAX_SESSIONS_TOTAL` is **20,000** (`web/storefront/src/lib/session.ts:105`) and
these cases create `MAX_SESSIONS_TOTAL + 50` sessions each. Every `createSession` does real
per-session token hashing, so a single case does ~20k hashes. `web/storefront` sets **no
`testTimeout`**, so all four run against vitest's **5s default**, and the file needs 15–50s
depending on machine load. Alone on an idle machine the file can pass (observed: 29 passed in
15.6s); under the gate's parallel load it does not.

**Why this is a real defect, not just slow tests.** It fails **open in the other direction** from
TKT-218: a timeout is reported as a failure, so the gate stays honest — but it makes `make check`
non-deterministic on machine load, which means **no ticket can be certified green reliably**. That
is the same blocking property TKT-198 was raised for.

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] The four cases pass deterministically under a loaded `make check`, three consecutive runs.
- [ ] The fix does NOT weaken what they prove — the global bound, the refusal at capacity, the
      rotate-at-own-cap path, and recovery after capacity frees. `MAX_SESSIONS_TOTAL` must still be
      exercised as a real bound, or the reduction argued explicitly.
- [ ] Whether the right fix is a per-file `testTimeout`, a smaller injectable cap for the test, or a
      faster hash in the test path is a plan decision — but note **a smaller cap is a fixture
      change**: ask what the reduced fixture can still distinguish (`AGENTS.md`, "a fixture too
      small cannot show the negative").

**Suggested direction (not a decision):** an injectable cap is the most honest — it keeps the
assertion about the real boundary while making the boundary cheap. Raising the timeout alone hides
that the suite takes ~50s for four cases.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed by **TKT-198**'s `agent:coding` stage (gateless run, 2026-08-08) as an incidental: it blocked that ticket's gate but is not its defect. Per the triage rule, incidentals become new backlog tickets rather than scope creep. Not shaped — needs `shaping.md` before Gate 1.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness — READY (shaped 2026-08-08)

**⚠ Gateless run.** Gate 1 waived by the owner along with the other three; shaped and moved to
`Ready` in one step. Same waiver terms as TKT-198 — recorded in the claim comment.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | OK | Deterministic under load, without weakening the assertions |
| Scope | OK | The test file + a minimal injectable seam |
| Uncertainties | WARN (deferred) | Mechanism choice, alternatives named — a plan decision |
| Dependencies | OK | None; this blocks TKT-198 |
| Approach | OK | **Narrowed during shaping — see below** |
| AC verifiable | OK | Three green loaded runs + a mutation check per test |
| Context-mémo | OK | Baked today |

#### What shaping found, so the plan does not have to rediscover it

**The cost is not crypto — it is quadratic.** The ticket as filed guessed "real per-session token
hashing". That is wrong: `createSession` mints its token with one `randomBytes(32)`, which is
microseconds. The expense is that **every** `createSession` walks the **entire** map
(`session.ts:224-231`) to sweep expired entries and collect the caller's own tokens. Filling to
20,000 is therefore ~200,000,000 iterations per test, four times over. The ticket's own description
should be read with that correction.

**This makes the choice much clearer than it looked:**

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Injectable cap** (recommended) | Removes the quadratic term. Every assertion still concerns the real boundary — refusal at capacity, the global bound, own-cap rotation, recovery — because those are properties of the *rule*, not of the number 20,000 |
| Raise `testTimeout` | Hides that four cases take ~50s. The suite stays quadratic and gets slower as anything else lands. Treats the symptom |
| Make `createSession` cheaper | A real optimization but a **production change** to a security-relevant path, to fix a test. Out of proportion, and `AGENTS.md` warns a bounded/optimized replacement is a new implementation needing its own review |

#### The trap this ticket must not fall into

`AGENTS.md`: *a fixture too small cannot show the negative.* Lowering the cap **is** shrinking the
fixture, so each of the four tests must be re-proved able to fail:

1. `bounds the map globally, across unlimited distinct principals` — needs **more distinct
   principals than the cap**, or it observes nothing. This is the one most at risk.
2. `refuses a new session at capacity rather than evicting a live one` — needs a live victim and a
   genuinely full map.
3. `lets a customer at their own cap rotate...` — needs `MAX_SESSIONS_PER_CUSTOMER` to still fit
   inside the reduced global cap. **A cap below 5 silently destroys this test.**
4. `accepts new sessions again once capacity frees up` — needs room to free.

**The mutation check is mandatory and per-test**: break the behaviour each one pins, one at a time,
observe red, restore. A cap small enough to be fast but too small to fail is the exact defect this
ticket would otherwise introduce while looking green.

binding.rule: A fixture too small cannot show the negative. A bounded or optimized replacement is a new implementation, so ask what the version it replaced would have caught.

governingAdrs.why: Customer identity and storefront sessions - the session map these caps bound. The global cap exists because registration is PUBLIC, so the per-principal cap bounds nothing on its own.
Public customer surface rate limiting (TKT-224). The session cap and the rate limiter are the two halves of the same flood story; the tests say 'neither is a fix; TKT-224 is'.

reference.summary: The four slow cases and the review passes that earned them - each comment names the finding it pins.
createSession walks the WHOLE map on every call (the sweep + per-principal collect), so filling the cap is O(n^2) - this is the cost, not crypto.
Existing test seam convention in the same module: resetSessionsForTest / sessionCountForTest.

objective.note: The four session-cap cases pass deterministically under a loaded `make check`, without weakening what they prove.

scope.note: web/storefront/test/session.test.ts and whatever minimal seam in src/lib/session.ts makes the cap injectable. Not the cap's VALUE in production, not the rate limiter.

uncertainties.note: Which mechanism: injectable cap (shaping's recommendation), per-file testTimeout, or a cheaper createSession. Named with their trade-offs below; a plan decision, not a shaping gap.

dependencies.note: None. Blocks TKT-198, which is why it runs first.

approach.note: Narrowed during shaping: make MAX_SESSIONS_TOTAL INJECTABLE for tests and drive the four cases at a small cap. The cost is O(n^2) - createSession walks the whole map every call - so 20,000 entries is ~200M iterations. Lowering the cap in the TEST removes the quadratic blowup while keeping every assertion about the real boundary. The module already has a *ForTest seam convention to follow.

first_slice.note: All four cases driven at a small injectable cap, each still asserting the same property it asserts today.

success.note: Deterministic: the four cases pass under a loaded gate, three consecutive `make check` runs, and each test still FAILS when the behaviour it pins is broken (mutation-checked, one at a time).
